comments.subject: Mojave Hotel Project
comments.comment:
The proposed hotel in the SunRiver area is a concern for the residents of this community. A hotel like this will bring additional traffic, more noise, impact the privacy of the community, and with additional travelers staying close to a retirement community, the safety of the residents can be impacted.

We request that the council reject the proposal due to these concerns.

Ryan and Kathryn Ockey

Sent from Samsung Galaxy smartphone

comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
Dear City Council Members,

In light of the recent fires in California, I am writing to express safety concerns for residential developments that only have one point of entry and exit. We live in similar circumstances with limited precipitation and dry landscapes and are at a high fire risk. My home is located on top of a bluff with a single point of entry and exit. Should a need arise where we would have to evacuate in a timely or even quick matter there would be grid lock and no way to evacuate off of the bluff. Please consider safety and evacuation plans for future potential hazards.

Thank you for your time

Sierra Sundloff

comments.subject: Public Comments Form
comments.comment:
This comment pertains to new city code for building retaining walls.

I have been attempting to get a permit to build a retaining wall on the front street facing side of my property because the house is on a hill and the erosion is going to eventually cause issues with the foundation of the home.

I have been told that the city code for retaining walls recently changed, and that it now requires a permit for certain conditions.

However anytime I submit an application it gets denied, and when I attempt to call, I am told that the retaining wall must be at least 10 feet back from the sidewalk.

However, the code clearly states that if the retaining wall is less than 4ft (the one I am planning on constructing is 3 ft 6 inches at the highest point), then it only needs to be set back 5 feet from the back of the sidewalk.

(for reference read section C at this URL: https://stgeorge.municipal.codes/Code/10-18-2)

Despite what the code says, I have been told multiple times that I cannot build because it must be 10 feet back from the sidewalk.

I would like some clarification on this, and clarification if I even need a permit at all for a wall that is less than four feet.

If I do need a permit, could someone please call me back or set up a time to speak with me? I have had the most difficult time getting ahold of anyone at the building department.

I have attached a pdf to show best I can the current state and desired outcome. I have contractors ready to go as soon as I get the ok from the city on this.

comments.subject: Re: January 2, 2025 - Atikinville Interchange - Hotel project
comments.comment:
I want to thank you for the time, presentation and very thoughtful discussion regarding the Mojave Project. I especially appreciated your comments and concerns of homeowners.

I was very disappointed in the Comments made by Mr. Tucker Nipco, who only met with a couple of people and did not listen, accept or feel any compassion or empathy to the two or three people he met. In fact, he said he did not need our support and did not feel he needed or wanted our support. I was not at the meeting, however he called me personally and after I raised a concern, he hung up on me - I could only assume he was looking for an ally to support his desires to develop this property. My only thought was can I trust a person who deals with people in this manner? Since Tucker did not want to work with Sunriver, he missed the opportunity to present his project to the Community (in our ballroom), just as Smith's, Big Shots, Les Schwab and others have done.

My one question is why does there need to be a second entry/exit for this property? We have many businesses in our community with only one entry/exit? Why not make the entry/exit on Pioneer (put a wall along Sand Piper) and move forward? I'm still in opposition, however I will SUPPORT the decision you make for our great city!

Thank you again for all you do for us little people!

Steve Lindley

p.s. I'm here to do what I can to protect those who are in the 80's and 90's that want to have a safe and secure final days of their lives in this great community and City of St. George.

[Quoted from earlier email, Mon, 30 Dec 2024 at 10:57]

Regarding: 5. Consider approval of Ordinance No. 2025-001 amending 5.06 acres of the Atkinville Interchange Area Commercial PD-C for a 107-room hotel, a 23,000 square foot medical...

Over the past six years I have been part of the Sunriver community working with developers to find positive solutions to Development in the SunRiver / Atkinville Interchange. We have developed many positive relationships and I hope to see more collaboration for services that would meet the needs of our growing city. Unfortunately, we have discovered the zoning was changed in (2018) the Atkinville Interchange that would allow hotels and even more concerning businesses that operate 24 hrs/day 7 days/week. Building hotels and any other businesses that would operate 24hrs/day 7days/week "east of Pioneer" offers a quiet zone and buffer to residents that would experience greater safety and security to all residents of Sunriver. Building west of Pioneer would be detrimental to the Residents of SunRiver. The concerns include: parking, safety, security, noise, right of privacy, etc.

I was very surprised to see an officer of the Law (who was not part of the Sunriver residents at the meeting) stand up and speak to the Planning Commission regarding the hotel. He stated this would be a safety and security problem for the 55 Plus community (please read his transcript from the meeting).

I believe that Parking was not given due to consideration that would be necessary for this hotel. This would leave the city streets to be used for large vehicles, towing recreational toys, worker trailers, semi trailers and people traveling with multiple vehicles. These vehicles would end up lining Sand Piper Dr, due to the entry and exit along Sand Piper Dr.

SPECIAL Considerations:
The Planning Commission asked the Mohave developer to rotate their hotel 90 degrees to prevent the hotel rooms from looking into our backyards - while this is a positive step, it's still not enough. There is no need for entry/exit on Sand Piper Dr, many commercial business have one entry/exit and this should only be on Pioneer Rd. In addition there should be a 6 foot wall on Sand Piper Dr further shielding the residential area and preventing all types of parking that would be disruptive to the Residents. This wall should also include part or all of NightHawk and perhaps even on the southside, if this property. The trash storage area would be better suited on the Southeast corner of the property away from any disruption while trash when being picked up, it would reduce the foul odors and noise.

My last concern is if this hotel is approved, we could easily see a number of Hotels built on the property between the Mojave hotel and the Fire Station. This would be extremely detrimental to SunRiver's quiet enjoyment, safety and security of our community. My reasoning for this statement is the owners of these properties have had them up for sale for over 8 years with few buyers, the property is being sold at three times the price of property in Desert Color. It seems this makes the only profitable businesses that could be developed in my backyard would be hotel's.

Sunriver has worked to the benefit of all with a number of developers in our area to support and come up with reasonable solutions to address concerns. We look forward to many more businesses that would serve our community and those at the southern end of St George! (Smith's, Les Schwab, Del Taco and we hear In & Out, StarBucks, Cafe Rio, a Hotel east of Pioneer and others yet to come and are excited to see them in our neighborhood)

Please do all you can to protect the Residents of SunRiver St. George Community Association.

Thank you for reading my suggestions and concerns. Thank you for your service to our great city of St. George!

Steve Lindley
